page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.6xlarge is a compute instance belonging to the High Clock Speed server family, powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor built on x86_64 architecture. Virtualized on a KVM hypervisor, it provides 24 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system features 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for vector instructions including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. Memory capacity is configured at 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The server includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local storage disks, and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance consistently within the middle 50 percent across compute and data-handling metrics. Synthetic CPU throughput measures 22989.57 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 23604.52 in PassMark CPU evaluations, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 9712.0. Memory throughput reaches 107.74 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 49.67 GB/sec for large block writes. In application-focused metrics, the instance achieves 22.01 million operations per second in Redis SET routines, 17.19 GB/sec in static web throughput, and 18813.0 in Clang software compilation benchmarks.

From an efficiency perspective, the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides substantial resource density for workloads demanding high memory capacity alongside sustained clock frequencies. A primary design tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning operational data persistence relies entirely on network-attached block devices. Supported instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI enable small-scale deep learning tasks, demonstrated by 79.94 tokens per second on 135M parameter LLM inference. Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.6xlarge is technically appropriate for in-memory databases, Redis caches, complex CI/CD build servers, and memory-intensive enterprise backend applications.
